absent: Module load, resolve, relocate, init invocation and unload sequencing beyond state names.
Locking order and required context for module list, sysfs and tree lookup mutations.
Allocator, protections and lifetime for per-class memory extents and percpu storage.
Format and consumers of modinfo tags, device-table matching and firmware loading.
Livepatch application, signature verification, taint assignment and unload refcount transitions.
Sysfs permission enforcement and value parsing for each parameter type.

findings.text: The module sysfs anchor groups a kobject with a back pointer to its module, an optional drivers directory, a parameter attribute set, and a completion used for lifetime coordination. Layout randomisation is requested for the container.

Module sysfs attributes pair a generic attribute with show and store handlers plus optional setup, test and free hooks tied to module lifetime. The version specialisation extends that pair with module name and version strings for read-only exposure.

Module startup and shutdown registration has two build configurations. One routes through generic init and exit registration helpers. The other exposes conventional init and cleanup entry names as aliases of the supplied handlers after a lightweight type compatibility check and marks them addressable in init and exit storage.

In the configuration shown, all staged boot entry macros from early through late plus console collapse to the same module initialisation registration, so callers cannot rely on distinct ordering levels from these fragments alone.

A module progresses from unformed during setup to coming while its initialisation runs, then to live for normal operation, and finally to going during removal. Liveness checks treat every state except going as still usable, while coming is true only during initialisation.

Module memory is partitioned into core text, data, read-only data and read-only-after-init plus init text, data and read-only data, with a count sentinel and a negative invalid value. Helper predicates distinguish init versus core, text versus data, and the core-data subset, with iterators over all types or over one class.

Each memory class records a base pointer, a read-execute flag and a size, optionally extended with a tree node for lookup builds. A companion node binds a module pointer to a latch tree node for address-indexed search.

The central module descriptor aggregates lifecycle state, global list linkage, fixed-size name, sysfs objects and version metadata, exported symbol tables with checksums and flags, parameter table, taint flags, init entry, per-class memory extents, architecture data, and many conditionally compiled subsystems such as exception tables, kallsyms, percpu, tracing, livepatch, unload refcount and exit entry. It requests cacheline alignment and layout randomisation.
Symbol metadata for a module holds a symbol table with count plus string and type tables. Livepatch metadata holds an ELF header copy with section headers, section names and symbol table index.

Address ownership is tested by range comparison against one class base and size, then by scanning the core or init classes, then by accepting either region. The no-module configuration short-circuits all region tests to false.
Liveness predicates report live unless removal has started and coming only during initialisation; the no-module variant always reports not coming and module iteration does nothing.

Reference handling in these fragments is degenerate and configuration dependent. One variant accepts a null module or a live module while leaving put and get empty; another always reports success. Symbol release operations are empty, symbol acquisition either pins a name against trimming and resolves by name or degrades to a hidden weak reference, and a request helper combines acquisition with on-demand loading.

Module information macros attach alias, dependency, licence, author, description, firmware, namespace, device-table and version tags to the modinfo area. One version configuration additionally instantiates a read-only version sysfs record naming the module and delegating display to a dedicated show routine, while the device-table helper creates a used alias object through a uniquified internal name.

Parameter handling centres on an operations table with set, get and optional free plus a no-argument flag, and a descriptor carrying name, owner, operations, permissions, level and option flags with a union for opaque argument, string or array. Strings bound length and buffer; arrays bound capacity, element size, live count, element operations and storage. Declaration helpers add compile-time type checking and type-name recording.

When sysfs is enabled the module descriptor carries a mutex dedicated to parameter access. The kallsyms view is documented as guarded by RCU and the module mutex, requiring RCU-aware dereference rather than plain loads.

Stated constants include a module name length derived from 64 minus pointer size, a no-argument operations flag, unsafe and hardware parameter flags, a GPL-only export flag, include guards for signature, symbol, loader and parameter headers, and empty versus dotted module-name prefixes for parameter and info tags.

The generic loader relocation entries always log an unsupported-relocation diagnostic naming the module and fail with an exec-format error, so any real relocation needs an architecture override. The no-module kallsyms and address lookup shims return neutral failures such as zero, out-of-range or not-supported without populating caller buffers.

Many queries degrade to constant answers when module support is absent: text, address, percpu and region tests report false or null, name reporting falls back to a kernel literal with null build identifier unless build-id support exists, notifier registration reports success, signature enforcement reports disabled with signature-ok true, retpoline validation reports true, and bug finalisation, bug cleanup, init-free flushing and module printing do nothing. Async-probe and livepatch predicates reflect stored flags only when their features are enabled.
Mapping symbols are recognised by distinctive short prefixes: dot followed by L, L followed by zero, or a leading dollar sign.

Init-section markers and module-memory alignment expand either to real attributes or to nothing depending on build mode, and the file tag for licence metadata is either empty or a file info record. Architecture init defaults to empty, stringification delegates to the generic helper, symbol value reads the ELF value field, and kthread exit either accounts the current module or exits directly.
